5. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

6. Place about 1/2 cup beef mixture on a cabbage leaf. Roll cabbage around beef mixture, tucking in sides to create an envelope around the meat. Repeat with remaining leaves and meat mixture. Place cabbage rolls in a layer atop the chopped cabbage in the casserole dish; season rolls with salt and black pepper.
7. Whisk tomato soup, tomato juice, and ketchup together in a bowl. Pour tomato soup mixture over cabbage rolls and cover dish wish aluminum foil.
8. Bake in the preheated oven until cabbage is tender and meat is cooked through, about 1 hour.
title: Golabki (cabbage roll)

steps: 1. In a medium bowl mix egg yolks, philly cheese and baking powder using a hand held mixer. Carefully start adding the flour. When the mixture will not be mixing well, and will look like wood chips, put away the blending mixer and using your hands knead the dough.
2. Create a roll and cover in foil and freeze for 15 minutes. At this time preheat the oven to 375.
3. Take the dough out and separate into two. Roll and cut out 3 inch trangles.
4. Make as many as you can and on centre of each put a small spoon of jam. Roll them into a croissant shape.
5. Place the croissants onto a greased cookie sheet, and bake for 10-12 minutes or until golden.
6. Repeat with the rest of the dough.
7. When you take them out, put aside and sprinkle with powdered sugar on top.
8. This makes about 3 batches of 20 cookies each.
9. Total count about 60 cookies.
title: Rogaliki (Polish Croissant Cookies)

steps: 1. Combine the yeast, a pinch of the sugar and a couple tablespoons of lukewarm water in a small bowl. Stir to dissolve the yeast, then leave for 10 mins until foamy.

2. Meanwhile, combine the flour, the remaining sugar and 2 tsp fine salt in a large bowl. Make a well in the centre, then add half the beaten egg, the yeast mixture and the oil. Pour in 200ml lukewarm water (it should feel slightly warm to the touch) and stir with a spoon, then mix using one hand, keeping the other clean while you bring the dough together. If there are a lot of very dry bits, gradually add a little water to just bring it together – you don't want it to get too wet and sticky. The dough should be moist, but not soggy.

3. Once the dough has come together, turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead using both hands for 10 mins until smooth and a bit springy. If it gets very sticky, add a very small amount of flour – as little as possible. A dough scraper is useful if the dough is sticking to the work surface. Stretch the sides of the dough down and pull together to form a ball. Lightly oil a bowl, then lightly roll the dough ball around the bowl so it's coated in the oil. Cover with a clean tea towel and leave in a warm place for 1 hr, or until dough has doubled in size.

4. Line a baking sheet with baking parchment. Turn the dough out onto a clean work surface and divide into three equal pieces, weighing for accuracy, if you like. Roll each piece into a long sausage shape about 25cm long, tapering them slightly at both ends. Lay the pieces out in front of you, parallel to one another with a couple centimetres between each. Bring the sausages together at the top end, then plait them down the length, tucking in the ends when you reach the bottom. Carefully transfer the loaf to the prepared baking sheet and loosely cover with a clean tea towel. Leave to rise until puffy and billowy, about 40 mins.

5. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Gently brush the rest of the beaten egg all over the challah, getting it into all the crevices, and sprinkle with the poppy or sesame seeds, if using. Bake on a middle shelf of the oven for 25-30 mins, until the loaf is golden brown underneath and sounds hollow when tapped. Check after about 15 mins – if the top of the loaf has started to get too dark, cover it with foil. Leave to cool on a wire rack, then serve.
title: Challah

steps: 1. Heat the oven to 170C/150C fan/gas 3½. Line a 30 x 22cm shallow baking tin with baking parchment. Sift the flour and mix it with cocoa, then set aside. Beat the egg whites until stiff, then add the sugar to them in small batches. Add the egg yolks, one by one, whisking constantly. Tip in the flour mixture and gently fold everything together with a spatula. Pour the prepared batter into the lined tin and bake for 35 mins. Cool for 5 mins, remove from the tin and re-line the tin with baking parchment.

2. To make the meringue, whisk the whites until stiff, then gradually whisk in the sugar, one tablespoon at a time. When you have a stiff and shiny meringue, fold in the finely chopped walnuts, flour and startch. Spread the mixture into the re-lined tin and cook for 40 mins on the same heat. Remove from the oven and leave to cool.
3. For the chocolate glaze, heat the cream over low heat, then remove from the heat, pour the chopped chocolate into it and mix it until it melts and becomes shiny.

4. Cut the cooled chocolate sponge cake and meringue into two layers. Put the nut meringue on top of the bottom layer of sponge and sprinkle on some of the reserved walnuts. Add another layer of meringue and then the upper layer of chocolate sponge cake and cover the top with chocolate glaze. Decorate with walnuts. Put the finished cake in the fridge for 1-2 hrs before serving.
title: Polish chocolate & walnut cake

steps: 1. Heat oven to 160C/140C fan/gas 3. Grease and line the base and sides of a deep 20cm cake tin with baking parchment. Put the honey, sugar and butter in a medium saucepan and cook over a medium heat until fully melted. Remove from the heat and allow to cool. Put the flour and spices in a large bowl and mix everything together.

2. Once the liquid ingredients have cooled, whisk in the eggs. Pour over the dry ingredients, whisking them together to form a smooth batter – be careful not to overmix as this can lead to a dry cake. Pour into the prepared tin and bake for 50-55 mins or until risen and a skewer inserted into the middle of the cake comes out clean. Allow the cake to cool in the pan for 20 mins before turning out onto a wire rack to cool completely.

3. Once cooled, use a large serrated knife to slice the cake into 3 layers. Spread the jam across the 2 bottom cake layers, then reassemble the cake and set aside while you make the glaze. Put the cream, chocolate and honey in a medium pan and cook over a low-medium heat until the chocolate is melted and you have a smooth, pourable mixture. Put the cake on a wire rack set over a parchment-lined baking tray and pour over the glaze, making sure to cover the entire cake. Use a fish slice to carefully transfer the cake to a serving plate and allow the glaze to set. To decorate, dust with a little edible gold powder, if you like. Uniced, this cake will keep for up to 5 days. Once iced, enjoy within 3 days – just keep in the fridge, but remove before serving and eat at room temperature.
title: Piernik (Polish gingerbread)

steps: 1. Preheat the oven to 180°C. (350˚F) Grease a cake pan and line it with baking paper.
2. In a large bowl, break the four eggs with the sugar and beat until they have tripled in volume and become fluffy.
3. Sift the self-rising baking flour and add it to your egg mixture. Fold this over, preserving as much air as possible. Add the melted (and slightly cooled) butter and mix until combined.
4. Add cinnamon, pinch of salt and vanilla extract.
5. Add the diced apple to the batter and gently fold them into the batter so that the apple pieces are evenly distributed. You can roll the apple pieces through some more cinnamon.
6. Pour the batter into the prepared cake pan and smooth the top with a spatula.
7. Place the apple slices on top of the batter and press lightly. Sprinkle optionally with some almond shavings.
8. Bake the apple cake in the preheated oven for about 45-50 minutes, or until a wooden skewer comes out clean when inserted into the center of the cake.
9. Remove the cake from the oven and let it cool in the mold for a few minutes. Then carefully remove the cake from the mold and let cool completely on a wire rack.
10. Sprinkle the cooled apple cake with powdered sugar
title: Apple cake

steps: 1. First, make the crispy shallots. Heat the oil in a saucepan to 180C (a cube of bread will turn golden in 15 secs). Toss the shallots in a little flour and deep-fry for 1 min or until light golden and crispy. Drain on kitchen paper. Can be made up to two days before and kept in an airtight container.
2. To make the filling, heat the oil in a medium non-stick frying pan and gently fry the shallots for 10 mins until starting to turn golden.

3. Add the sauerkraut and cabbage, and cook for 5-10 mins until the cabbage has softened. Taste and add a little salt if under-seasoned, or sugar if stringent. Scrape into a bowl and leave to cool completely.

4. To make the dough, mix the eggs and oil with 125ml water, then gradually add in the flour, mixing well with your hands. Knead it on a well-floured surface until the dough stops sticking to your hands. You should end up with firm, elastic dough. Wrap it in cling film and rest in the fridge for at least 30 mins, or overnight.
5. Flour your work surface generously. Roll out the dough to a 40cm circle or until the dough is as thick as £1 coin.

6. Using a 9cm cookie cutter, cut out discs in the dough – you should end up with about 25 discs. Do not throw away the off-cuts – we throw them in with the pierogi when boiling to minimise any waste.

7. Have a well-floured tray ready. Put 1 tsp of the filling into the centre of each disc. In your hand, fold in half around the filling and seal to create half-moon shapes. Put them on the floured tray, making sure they don’t touch each other.
8. Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil and carefully lower the pierogi in. Boil them for 2 mins or until they float to the top.
9. Drain and serve with a knob of butter and some soured cream. Finish by sprinkling the crispy shallots on top to serve.
title: Sauerkraut pierogii

ingredients.text: 1 cup yogurt(thick Greek variety is best)

steps: 1. Spray 9" spring form pan with nonstick spray.
3. Combine 1 c. flour, 1/2 c. sugar and baking powder in a medium bowl. Add butter, egg and vanilla. Stir till well mixed, spread on bottom of pan, sprinkle w/ berries.
5. Combine yogurt, sugar, egg, flour ,lemon peel and vanilla and mix until smooth. Pour over berries.
7. Bake at 350 degrees for 35 minutes or until center appears to be set when shaken. Cool 15 minutes. Remove sides. Cool completely for 2-4 hours. Serves 8-10.
title: Kuchen

steps: 1. Mix ground beef, egg, rice, onion, carrot, salt and pepper. Mix together vinegar, brown sugar and tomato sauce.
2. Drop cabbage into boiling water for 5 to 10 minutes.
3. Remove 10 large leaves. Chop remaining cabbage and place in bottom of crock-pot.
4. Place 2 to 4 tablespoons of meat mixture in center of each leaf.
5. Roll up and use toothpick to hold.
6. Place stem side down in crock-pot. Pour on tomato mixture.
7. Cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours. Serves 6 to 8.
title: Crock-Pot Polish Cabbage Rolls

steps: 1. Mix sugar, vinegar and oil well.
2. Pour over remaining ingredients; toss.
3. Cover and chill 3 to 24 hours.
4. Makes 6 to 8 servings.
5. Great side dish with brats or Polish sausage.
title: Sweet Sauerkraut Salad

steps: 1. Finely chop potatoes.
2. Dry with paper towels.
3. Mix eggs, flour, onion and potatoes.
4. Make into a dough.
5. Heat approximately 2 tablespoons oil in pan on medium heat.
6. Drop heaping tablespoonfuls of potato mixture in pan and fry on both sides until light brown.
7. Serve with applesauce or other fruit.
8. Serves 4.
title: German Potato Pancakes

steps: 1. Preheat oven to 305°.
2. Grease an 8 x 8-inch square pan. Combine butter, sugar and eggs in large bowl and beat thoroughly. Add flour, baking powder and vanilla and beat until well blended. Spread evenly in pan.
3. Combine sugar and cinnamon.
4. Peel and core apples and thinly slice into large bowl.
5. Add sugar-cinnamon mixture to taste, coating apples thoroughly.
6. Arrange slices on top of batter in overlapping rows, pressing lightly into batter. Bake 1 hour.
7. Cool and cut into squares.
8. Makes 6 to 8 servings.
title: German Apple Cake

steps: 1. Mix beef, egg, milk, crumbs, onion and seasonings to make meat loaf; mold into ring in 2-quart round baking dish.
2. Parboil cauliflower, place in center of meat loaf.
3. Mix cheese and milk, pour over cauliflower.
4. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to one hour, last 5 minutes of baking place tomatoes on top of meat loaf. Yields 4 servings.
title: German Meat Loaf

steps: 1. Core cabbage and place in enough boiling salted water to cover. With a fork in one hand and a knife in the other, keep cutting off the leaves as they become wilted; drain. Trim thick center veins of each cabbage leaf. Brown onion in shortening. Add to meat, seasonings and rice. Mix well. Place a tablespoon of filling onto each cabbage leaf and roll; tuck in edges. Place in pot and cover 2/3 full with water. Add tomato sauce and ketchup. Cover and cook slowly for about 1 1/2 hours until rice is tender. Serves 6 to 8 people.
title: Hungarian Stuffed Cabbage Rolls

steps: 1. Soften gelatin in 1/4 cup of the orange juice and heat over hot water.
2. Combine remaining 1 1/4 cups orange juice with sugar.
3. Add gelatin and set in cold place, stirring occasionally to dissolve sugar.
4. When mixture is set to a soft jelly, whip the cream until stiff.
5. Fold in lemon juice and then orange gelatin mixture.
6. Pour into mold and set.
7. Serves 8.
title: Orange Bavarian Dessert

steps: 1. Put the butter in a bowl that has been rinsed out with very hot water, so the butter will soften slightly.
2. Add 1/2 cup sugar and 1 egg and stir briskly until well mixed.
3. Add the second egg and beat until light.
4. Add the flour and salt; mix well and spread in deep pie plate or casserole.
5. Arrange halves of plums, skin side down, on the batter and sprinkle with the remaining 1/2 cup sugar and cinnamon.
6. Bake at 400° for 30 minutes.
7. Serve plain or with whipped cream to which a little fruit syrup has been added. Serves 6.
title: German Plum Cake

steps: 1. Saute onions in margarine until transparent, set aside to cool. Cook Minute rice as directed on box and set aside to cool. Carefully break leaves from cabbage head so as to keep leaves from tearing.
2. Wash leaves.
3. Drop leaves in boiling water just long enough to make pliable.
4. In large bowl, mix together pork, beef, onion, rice and Worcestershire sauce.
5. Shape mixture into 8 oval "loaves."
6. Wrap each loaf with a cabbage leaf and place in 8 x 10-inch casserole dish.
7. Squeeze tomatoes and juice over each loaf. Stick in bay leaves.
8. Bake, covered, at 325° for 1 1/2 to 2 hours. Serves 6 to 8.
title: Cabbage Rolls

steps: 1. Preheat oven to 450°. Whisk eggs until blended. Sift flour, measure and sift again with salt. Add flour mixture to beaten eggs in 4 additions, beating after each addition just until mixture is smooth. Add milk in 2 additions, beating slightly after each. Lightly beat in melted butter. Using 2 tablespoons softened butter, butter bottom and sides of a 9 or 10-inch heavy skillet. Pour batter into skillet and bake at 450° for 20 minutes. Slip onto a heated platter and serve immediately. Makes 4 servings.
title: Baked German Pancake

ingredients.text: 1 1/2 c. instant tea (with lemon and sugar)

steps: 1. Mix and serve 2 heaping teaspoonfuls per cup of hot water.
title: Russian Tea

steps: 1. Mix lard, flour, white sugar and brown sugar with forks or fingers to form crumbs.
2. Take out 1 cup of crumbs; set aside for topping.
3. Beat eggs, sour milk and baking soda together.
4. Pour into a greased and floured pan.
5. Sprinkle crumbs on top and also cinnamon, if you want.
6. Bake at 300° until a toothpick comes out clean.
7. Serves 8.
title: Hungarian Coffee Cake

steps: 1. Cook the onion in the butter until it is tender but not brown.
2. Add the corn meal along with the salt, sugar, pepper, and cinnamon, and mix them to coat the cereal thoroughly with the butter.
3. Pour in the scalded milk gradually and stir briskly until the mixture is smooth and free of lumps.
4. Cook until it thickens.
5. Remove it from the range and blend in the cream.
6. Beat the eggs well and fold into the cereal.
7. Spoon into a 2-quart buttered casserole.
8. Bake the nachynka uncovered in a moderate oven (350 degrees F) for 1 hour.
9. It should have a crisp golden brown crust all around.
10. Serves 6 to 8.
title: Ukrainian Bukovinian Nachynka (Cornbread Dressing)

steps: 1. Mix well.
2. Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until done.
3. Frost with chocolate frosting.
title: Sauerkraut Cocoa Cake

steps: 1. Combine sugar, milk, eggs and oleo.
2. Mix together in pan and bring to boil.
3. Add vanilla, coconut and pecans.
4. Beat until thick and spread on cake.
title: German Chocolate Icing

steps: 1. Drain sauerkraut and squeeze dry.
2. Mix all ingredients (except cream cheese).
3. Shape into loaf or ball.
4. Chill overnight.
title: German Cheese Ball

steps: 1. Cream the butter and sugar.
2. Add vanilla.
3. Mix flour and salt together and add.
4. Chill the dough for about 10 minutes.
5. Roll into 1 inch balls, place on uncreased cookie sheet.
6. Bake until set, but not brown in 350 deg. for10-12 minutes.
7. While still warm, roll in confectioner's sugar.
8. Once cool, roll in sugar again. Then eat!
title: Best Russian Tea Cakes Ever

ingredients.text: 1 c. light brown sugar, firmly packed

steps: 1. Preheat oven to 350° and lightly grease and flour a 9-inch tube pan.
2. Into a large bowl, sift flour with baking powder, salt, cinnamon, sugars and coffee.
3. Using pastry blender or 2 knives, cut butter and shortening into flour mixture until it resembles small peas.
4. Set aside 1 cup for topping.
5. Combine milk with baking soda and eggs; mix well.
6. With wooden spoon, stir all at once into flour-fat mixture.
7. Bake 55 to 60 minutes, or until cake tester inserted in center comes out clean.
8. Let cool in pan for 10 minutes.
9. Remove from pan and serve warm.
title: Coffee Kuchen

steps: 1. Preheat oven to 375°F; put oven rack in middle position.

2. While oven is heating up, divide butter in half (1/4 cup each). Melt one of the halves. The other half, divide again, and place pieces in two large cast-iron or stone-ware frying pans. Place pans in oven while it preheats.
3. In a blender, mix melted butter, eggs, sugar, flour and milk.
4. Remove pans from oven, swirl butter around slightly up the side of the pans.
5. Pour half of the flour-milk mixture into the first pan, the remainder in the second pan.
6. Quickly return pans to the oven. Bake until fluffy, golden brown and crispy, about 45 minutes. The puffiness goes down as it cools. Serve immediately with Honey Butter (follows).
7. PREPARE HONEY BUTTER: While the pancakes are baking, rinse out blender; pour in warmed honey and start blender on medium-high.
8. Slowly drizzle in half of the 1/2 cup melted butter; mix for 10 seconds, then add remaining butter. Mix for 3 minutes (if you can stand the racket!).
9. Add cream and vanilla; blend/pulse just enough to mix it in .
10. This makes 1 1/2 cups and is best served warm.
11. Store leftover honey butter in fridge. Reheat for just a few seconds in the microwave--do NOT boil!
title: Gramma'S German Pancakes With Honey Butter

steps: 1. Mix all ingredients except nuts and coconut in saucepan and cook
3. minutes;
4. stirring
5. constantly.
6. Add
7. nuts
8. and coconut and beat

11. is of spreading consistency. Yield: Enough icing for a 2-layer cake.
title: German Chocolate Frosting

steps: 1. Mix butter, sugar and vanilla.
2. Sift in flour.
3. Add nuts. Roll into small bars and chill (about 1 teaspoon of dough).
4. Bake at 400° until lightly browned.
5. Roll in confectioners sugar while warm.
title: Russian Tea Cookies

steps: 1. Combine all ingredients in blender container.
2. Blend all together until well mixed.
3. Store in refrigerator.
title: Russian Dressing

steps: 1. Mix first three ingredients until crumbly.Remove 1/2 c mixture and mix with cinnamon and nuts. RESERVE for topping.
2. Add baking soda and baking powder to step 1 mixture and stir to mix it all in evenly.
3. Add vinegar to milk to sour the milk. Stir egg into the milk and stir vigorously with a fork to blend the egg. Add to the dry mixture and stir just until blended.
4. Spray or grease a 9x13 pan and pour mixture into pan. Top with reserved topping.
5. Bake at 350 degrees until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean, about 30 minutes.
title: Cinnamon Coffee Cake - Kaffeekuchen

steps: 1. Boil the raisins and water for 5 minutes and let cool. Then add the baking soda.
2. Creme together the butter, sugar, eggs.
3. Add other ingredients and raisins (make sure the raisins are completely cool).
4. Drop by small spoonfuls onto a baking sheet and press them flat.
5. Bake at 400°F until brown on edges.
6. Let sit on tray before transferring to a cooling rack.
title: Russian Tea Biscuits

steps: 1. Cook meat and drain real good.
2. Cube cheese and stir into meat until melted.
3. Add oregano and garlic (minced or salt) to taste. Spread on rye cocktail bread.
4. Place on cookie sheet and place in freezer on cookie sheets until frozen.
5. Then remove and place on foil in Tupperware containers and return to freezer until ready to use.
6. When ready to serve, place directly from freezer to oven. Bake at 350° for 10 minutes or microwave 1 minute or perhaps more, depending on oven.
title: Polish Mistakes

ingredients.text: 2 lb. sirloin steak, sliced into 2-inch long strips

steps: 1. Coat steak strips with mixture of flour, salt and pepper. Brown meat and onion in 1/3 cup butter.
2. Add beef bouillon and red wine and allow to simmer for 30 minutes.
3. While meat is simmering, cook sliced mushrooms in 3 tablespoons butter until soft.
4. When meat is tender, remove from heat.
5. Add mushrooms and stir. Combine sour cream, tomato paste and Worcestershire sauce and gradually add to meat and mushrooms.
6. Put back on heat and simmer. Do not boil.
7. Serve with rice.
title: Beef Stroganoff

ingredients.text: 1/2 lb. kielbasa, cut in half and thinly sliced

steps: 1. Grease a 2-quart casserole.
2. Heat oven to 375°.
3. Place potatoes in large pot of lightly salted water.
4. Cook until water comes to boil.
5. Simmer 10 minutes.
6. Remove potatoes and set aside. Add noodles to water and cook 5 minutes.
7. Drain and return to pot.
8. Heat butter and oil; add onion and cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender.
9. Add cooked potatoes, paprika and salt to onions.
10. Cook 2 minutes; add chicken broth and boil 1 minute.
11. Pour potato mixture over noodles and mix well.
12. Pour mixture in casserole.
13. Toss kielbasa over top.
14. Bake 20 minutes.
title: Kielbasa And Noodle Casserole

steps: 1. Combine first 3 ingredients in a large bowl. Weigh down cabbage with a smaller bowl filled with cans. Let stand at room temperature 24 hours, tossing occasionally.
2. Bring vinegar and next 4 ingredients (through allspice) to a boil in a large saucepan; reduce heat, and simmer 5 minutes. Cover and let stand at room temperature 24 hours.
3. Rinse cabbage thoroughly under cold water. Drain cabbage; squeeze dry. Place cabbage in large bowl.

4. Strain vinegar mixture through a colander over a bowl; discard solids. Stir 1 cup water and sugar into vinegar; pour over cabbage mixture, pressing down to immerse. Cover and refrigerate 5 days. Store in an airtight container in refrigerator up to 1 week.
title: Red Sauerkraut

steps: 1. Preheat the oven to 200°C/fan180°C/gas 6. fry sausages in a non-stick pan until browned.
2. Drizzle vegetable oil in a 30cm x 25cm x 6cm deep roasting tray and heat in the oven for 5 minutes.
3. Put the plain flour in a bowl, crack in the medium free-range eggs, then stir in the grated horseradish. Gradually beat in the semi-skimmed milk. Season.
4. Put the sausages into the hot roasting tray and pour over the batter. Top with cherry tomatoes on the vine and cook for 30 minutes until puffed and golden.
title: Toad In The Hole

steps: 1. Heat the oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6. Butter and line a 20 x 30cm rectangle tin.

2. Beat the butter and sugar in a free-standing mixer until pale and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time and beat well. Beat through the flour, milk and salt until fully combined, then spoon into the tin. Bake in the oven for 25 mins or until golden and firm to the touch. Set aside to cool completely.

3. Slice the sponge horizontally to create two halves. Trim the edges to make perfect corners. Cut the sponge into 18 squares. Lightly whip the cream with the icing sugar until it reaches soft peaks. Spread a little of the jam on half of the sponge squares then pipe or spread over a little of the cream. Sandwich each one with a second square of sponge then set aside in the fridge to chill.

4. To make the icing, whisk together the melted butter and milk in a bowl. Sieve the cocoa powder and icing sugar together in a seperate bowl. Gradually add the cocoa and sugar to the butter and milk mixture, whisking continuously to ensure there are no lumps. If it gets lumpy, whizz with a hand blender until smooth.
5. Divide the coconut between three shallow bowls (this keeps it from getting coated in too much chocolate whilst you’re dipping).
6. Dip each lamington in the icing until completely covered. Roll in the coconut and set on a wire rack. Repeat with the remaining sponges. Chill for a minimum of 1 hr.
title: Lamingtons

steps: 1. Sauté the onions:
2. Heat butter in a large skillet (preferably cast iron) on medium heat. Add the onion and cook a few minutes, until translucent.
3. Add the potatoes and corned beef:
4. Mix in the chopped corned beef and potatoes. Spread out evenly over the pan. Increase the heat to high or medium high and press down on the mixture with a metal spatula.
5. Cook until browned and then flip:
6. Do not stir the potatoes and corned beef, but let them brown. If you hear them sizzling, this is good.

7. Use a metal spatula to peek underneath and see if they are browning. If nicely browned, use the spatula to flip sections over in the pan so that they brown on the other side. Press down again with the spatula.
8. If there is too much sticking, you can add a little more butter to the pan. Continue to cook in this manner until the potatoes and the corned beef are nicely browned.
9. Stir in the parsley and season:
10. Remove from heat, stir in chopped parsley. Add plenty of freshly ground black pepper, and add salt to taste.
title: Corned Beef Hash

steps: 1. Beat eggs; add cheese and milk.
2. Pour mixture in a frying pan with butter.
3. Cook slowly stirring constantly.
4. When mixture has consistency of scrambled eggs, serve over toast.
5. Serves 4.
title: Welsh Rarebit

steps: 1. Wash the oranges and place them whole in a large pot, cover with water and bring to the boil (more water may be needed as stated depending on the size of your oranges and your pot). Simmer for 90 minutes (skins should be soft and easily pierced with a sharp knife).

2. Remove oranges from liquid and cool (keep the liquid). When cook enough to handle with your hands, cut in half and scoop out the pulp and place into a colander. Press down hard with the back of a spoon and add this to the water.

3. Slice the orange skins (thick or thin, you choose) and add to the pot. Stir in the sugar and place back on the heat. Stir until the sugar dissolves. Boil over a high heat for 15-20 minutes. Skim off any scum or froth that rises to the surface.
4. Test to see that the marmalade is set (a small spoonful on a fridge cold plate, it should "set" within 60 seconds). If not, cook some more and re-try for setting again.
5. Leave hot marmalade in the pot for 30 minutes and stir often, this stops the strips of peel don't sink to the bottom of the pot/jar.
6. Ladle into steralised jars. Marmalade will keep for 6 months in the pantry OR 2 weeks in the fridge once opened.
title: English Orange Marmalade

ingredients.text: 4 cups cabbage, chopped parboiled and drained well

steps: 1. Chop cooked, unpeeled potatoes.
2. In large skillet, fry bacon; drain on paper towel.
3. Saute onion and in bacon fat until golden brown.
4. Add chopped, precooked cabbage and chopped, cooked potatoes to the pan with the sauteed onions.
5. Chop the fried bacon and sprinkle the bits over top surface.
6. Allow potatoes to become golden brown on bottom over medium heat.
7. Invert skillet over large serving plate.
8. Garnish with parsley, if desired.
title: Simply English Bubble & Squeak

steps: 1. Cook and mash potatoes; fold in shredded cabbage and scallions that have been cooked with milk.
2. This recipe can be cut in half or doubled, depending on amount to feed.
title: Colcannon

steps: 1. Steam 2 cups of fresh peas for 10 minutes (or 2 cups of frozen peas for 1 minute). Toss with 1 tablespoon fresh mint (chiffonade), 3 tablespoons cream, and 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt.
title: English Peas

steps: 1. In a large saucepan, heat the milk & add the sugar - cook gently over a low heat, stirring well.
2. Add butter and cream of tartar. Boil until a little dropped into cold water hardens.
3. Pour into greased ramekins or pudding moulds and leave to set.
title: Doncaster Butterscotch - Traditional English!

steps: 1. Preheat oven to 300 degrees f.
2. Peel and quarter the parsnips and boil for 15 minutes, making sure not to let them cook completely. You want them to be par-boiled only.
3. Place the parsnips in a large dish and add the Beef Stock , salt, pepper
4. and nutmeg. Taste and add more salt, pepper and nutmeg, if required.
5. Top with butter and cook for 30 minutes on a low heat in the oven.
title: Baked Parsnips - Irish Recipe

steps: 1. Melt butter.
2. Add cornstarch & milk.
3. Cook for 5 minutes.
4. Add cheese and seasonings.
5. Serve on crackers or toast.
title: Welsh Rarebit

ingredients.text: 1/4 head cabbage, shredded and lightly steamed

steps: 1. Cook bacon slices in a large skillet and remove when crispy. Crumble and set aside.
2. Add onions to pan and gently fry until tender. Add potato and cabbage. Press together to form a large cake. Cook until first side is brown then turn with a spatula and brown the other side.
3. Slide out from pan and sprinkle with crumbled bacon.
4. Serve with toast and/or eggs.
title: Bubble And Squeak

steps: 1. Put all ingredients in a blender.
2. Blend until smooth.
3. Fill 8 well-greased muffin tins or custard cups.
4. Bake at 400° for 10 minutes, then lower oven temperature to 350° for 20 minutes longer.
5. Serve warm with butter and jam.
title: English Popovers

ingredients.text: 1/4 cup lemon, rind of, Finely grated

steps: 1. Pat pork dry.
2. Score well with sharp knife.
3. Combine parsley, onion, peel, basil, and garlic in a small bowl.
4. Whisk in 2/3 of oil.
5. Rub into pork.
6. Wrap in foil and refrigerate overnight.
7. Let pork stand at room temperature 1 hour before roasting.
8. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
9. Brush pork with remaining olive oil.
10. Set on rack in shallow pan.
11. Roast until meat thermometer inserted in thickest part of meat registers 170 degrees F, about 2 1/2 hours.
12. Set meat aside.
13. Degrease pan juices.
14. Blend Sherry into pan juices.
15. Cover and cook over low heat 2 minutes.
16. Pour into sauceboat.
17. Transfer pork to platter.
18. Garnish with fresh parsley and lemon slices.
19. Serve sauce separately.
title: Irish Loin Of Pork With Lemon And Herbs

steps: 1. Heat molasses to boiling point. Add oleo, then slowly, stirring constantly, add flour sifted with ginger and sugar. Drop small portions on greased inverted cookie pan 2-inches apart. Bake 15 minutes at 300°. Cool slightly. Remove from pan and roll over handle of wooden spoon. If they get too hard, put in oven for a second. Nuts may be added if desired.
title: English Rolled Wafers

ingredients.text: 2 heads cabbage, cored and cut into wedges

steps: 1. Rinse the beef brisket under cold water, and place in a large pot. Add enough water to cover the roast by 6 inches. Peel the onions, and place them in the pot with the roast. Bring to a boil, and cook for about 30 minutes at a rolling boil. Reduce heat to medium-low so that the water is at a gentle boil, cover, and cook for 3 1/2 hours.

2. Remove the lid from the brisket. Remove onions, and cut into wedges. Return them to the pot. Add carrots to the pot, then place the cabbage over the roast. Place the potatoes on top of the cabbage. Place the lid back on the pot, and cook for another 30 minutes, until potatoes are tender. The potatoes should be immersed in the water by now, but if not, keep the lid on so they can steam.
3. Remove the vegetables from the pot, and place in a separate serving bowl. Keep the corned beef in the pot until ready to slice and serve because it dries out quickly.
title: Irish Boiled Dinner (Corned Beef)

steps: 1. Cut meat into squares and cook slowly until tender.
2. Add vegetables.
3. Thicken with a little flour mixture.
title: Irish Stew

ingredients.text: 275 g fresh puff pastry, rolled out on baking parchment, 25cm x 42 cm
1 bunch parsley, finely chopped, some set aside for garnish

steps: 1. Preheat the oven to 400°F. Roll the puff pastry out on parchment paper to 10 x 16 inches.

2. For the herb crust: mix the breadcrumbs, Parmesan, butter, eggs and herbs into a smooth paste. Season to taste. Press the herb crust evenly around the turkey breast, then wrap the breast in the puff pastry. Cut off any excess pastry (use to cut out leaf or flower shapes for decoration, if desired). Beat the egg yolk with 3 tbsp of water and brush the pastry with egg mixture. Bake for 45-60 mins, testing for doneness. Cover with foil after about 40 mins of cooking.
3. Heat the oil in a pan and cook the gnocchi for 10 mins, stirring frequently. After 5 mins, stir in the tomatoes and season to taste. Stir in the pesto and 4 tbsp of water.
4. Serve the turkey with the gnocchi on the side, garnished with parsley.
title: Roast Turkey Wellington

steps: 1. Combine all ingredients to the hot rice and reheat for a few minutes.
2. Serve at once.
title: New England Kedgeree

steps: 1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease 2 baking sheets.
2. Combine flour, baking soda, and spices. In a large bowl, cream shortening and sugar. Beat in the egg. Beat in the corn syrup and cider vinegar. Gradually blend in the dry ingredients.

3. On a floured surface, roll out dough to a thickness of 1/4 inch. Using a 1 1/2 inch round cookie cutter, cut dough into rounds and place 1 1/2 inches apart on prepared baking sheets. Bake for 8-12 minutes--until firm to the touch. Transfer to wire racks to cool.
title: English Snaps

steps: 1. In a large skillet, melt butter over medium high heat. Add potatoes, onion and green pepper; saute until potatoes are browned. Stir in eggs and cook until eggs are set. Serve warm.
title: Irish Eggs

ingredients.text: 5 eggs (separated), beat egg whites and set aside

steps: 1. Mix flour and baking powder and set aside.
2. Cream sugar and butter.
3. Add yolks and beat until fluffy.
4. Mix flour with sugar mixture and milk alternately.
5. Add vanilla and fold in beaten egg whites. Bake at 350° for 45 minutes to 1 hour in a 9 x 13-inch pan.
title: Irish Rag

steps: 1. Sift dry ingredients into a bowl and mix well. Slowly add buttermilk and mix to a soft dough. Don't add all the buttermilk at once, in case you need a little less than the recipe states. Work quickly and lightly-don't overwork the dough!
2. Turn dough onto a floured work surface and roll out until approximately 1/2 inch thick. Cut into 4 farls.
3. Bake on a griddle or frying pan on a medium low heat for 15-20 minutes, turning once or twice. Remove when golden brown and wrap in a cloth until cool (this keeps the crust soft).
title: Traditional Irish Soda Farls

steps: 1. Mix yeast with the sugar.
2. Add water and let stand for 5 minutes until foamy.
3. Stir in the milk, egg and 1 tablespoon of the butter.
4. Add flour and salt.
5. Mix until well blended, cover with damp towel and let stand in warm place until doubled (about 45 minutes).
6. Brush the insides of 4 three-inch flan rings (or tuna fish cans with both ends removed) and the bottom of a heavy frying pan with melted butter.
7. Over low heat, heat the rings in the pan and then place about 2 tablespoons of batter into each.
8. Cook for 7 minutes, or until holes appear and the tops are dry.
9. Then remove the rings and turn the crumpets to brown them lightly on the other side (about 2 minutes).
10. Repeat the process with the remaining batter.
11. Crumpets are best served warm, but can be cooled on a wire rack and toasted just before serving.
12. Yield 6 crumpets.
title: Crumpets

ingredients.text: 8 whole Russet Potatoes, Peeled And Quartered

steps: 1. Begin by adding your potatoes to a large pot of water. Cover and bring to a boil, reducing the heat to medium, and slightly uncovered as to not boil over. Cook until fork tender, roughly 25 minutes.
2. In the meantime, add the milk and onions to a sauce pan, and cook on medium to low heat to warm everything through.
3. To another small pot of water, add the chopped kale, and bring to a boil, then cover, reducing the heat to a simmer, and cook for about 20 minutes.

4. Once the potatoes are fork tender, drain, and return them back to the pot on the stove. Allow the potatoes to cook, evaporating the rest of the water. Strain the kale and squeeze out any moisture by gently pushing on it with the back of a spoon.
5. Get your masher out and toss in the four tablespoons of butter. Add in the milk and onion mixture, and begin to mash into a nice creamy consistency. Season with salt and pepper, and mix again.
6. Add in the kale, and mix until everything is incorporated. Taste. Season with any additional salt and pepper.
7. To plate, add a bit to a small bowl, make an indention into the center, and add in one tablespoon of melted butter.

8. The Irish colcannon is really amazing. Like I said, the addition of kale, and the warmed onion and milk mixture make this truly comforting. Oh yeah, and if you are wanting to bring it up to another level, add a bit of cooked, crisp bacon. Well, that is for another day. Enjoy.
title: Irish Colcannon With Kale

steps: 1. Heat 1/4 cup butter in a 1-quart dish in 425° oven until it bubbles.
2. Meanwhile, beat eggs with milk, then gradually beat in flour and salt.
3. Pour batter into bubbling butter.
4. Drop rhubarb into center of batter.
5. Do not mix.
6. Bake in 425° oven for 25 minutes or until crust is brown.
title: Rhubarb Yorkshire

ingredients.text: 1 cup raspberries (other berries would work fine here)

steps: 1. Toast the oatmeal in a 400°F oven for 8 to 10 minutes. Let cool.
2. Beat the cream until it is soft, not stiff. Add and gently beat in the sugar and vanilla.
3. Fold in the cooled oatmeal and raspberries. Put into a serving dish, cover and chill. Enjoy!
title: Scottish Cream Crowdie With Raspberries

steps: 1. Brown ground beef.
2. Add potaoes and cabbage.
3. Cook until cabbage is translucent.
4. Spread on sheet pan and broil
5. Stir until desired crispiness.
title: Irish Hash

steps: 1. Place potatoes in a large saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat; cover and cook for 10-15 minutes or until tender.
2. Meanwhile, place cabbage in a small saucepan and cover with water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat; cover and simmer for 6-8 minutes or until tender.

3. Drain potatoes; mash with milk, salt and pepper. Set aside. In a large skillet, saute onions and leek in butter until tender. Drain cabbage; add to skillet with potato mixture. Heat through; sprinkle with parsley.
title: Irish Colcannon With Spring Onions And Leeks

steps: 1. Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2. Cream sugar, egg, salt and shortening together. Add flour, baking soda and spices. Mix well. Roll teaspoonfuls of dough into balls and roll the balls in sugar.
3. Bake at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 5 to 6 minutes.
title: Irish Ginger Snaps

steps: 1. Whip eggs; add all ingredients.
2. Stir well and pour into containers.
3. Store in refrigerator right away.
4. For a richer taste, double recipe and add small bottle inexpensive Irish cream.
title: Irish Cream

steps: 1. Heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat until hot. Add onion; cook 4 minutes or until tender, stirring often.
2. Add mushrooms to skillet; cook 4 minutes or until tender, stirring often. Stir in peas and remaining ingredients; cover and cook 4 minutes or just until peas are tender. Serve immediately.
title: Herbed English Peas With Mushrooms

steps: 1. Preheat oven to 325
2. In a heavy skillet, heat the olive oil and brown the beef over medium high. Remove to casserole dish.
3. In same skillet, saute the vegetables until slightly browned.
4. Mix in the flour, then gradually add the stock. Mix in tomato paste and season to taste.
5. Mix all in casserole dish, cover and cook in the preheated oven for 45 minutes.
6. Place the thinly sliced potatoes on top, cover and continue cooking for a further 45 minutes or until the potatoes and meat are tender.
title: Irish Beef Stew

steps: 1. Mix all ingredients together and store in an air-tight container.
title: Scottish Mixed Spice

ingredients.text: 6 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into eighths

steps: 1. Cook cabbage, covered, in a small amount of boiling salted water 5 to 7 minutes or until tender.
2. Drain and set cabbage aside.
3. Cook potatoes in boiling salted water to cover 15 minutes or until tender.
4. Drain and mash.
5. Add butter and next 3 ingredients; mix well.
6. Add cabbage, stirring well.
7. Serve immediately.
title: Colcannon

ingredients.text: 4 lbs russet potatoes, peeled and quartered

steps: 1. Core and dice cabbage and put in 3 quart saucepan. Cover with water and bring to boil. Cook until tender, about 45 minutes.
2. Put potatoes in 4 quart saucepan. Cover with water and bring to boil. Cook until tender, about 20 minutes.
3. Thinly slice leeks. Put in 2 quart saucepan, add evaporated milk, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Boil until tender, about 10 minutes.
4. Drain potatoes and mash. Stir in leek mixture. Fold in drained cabbage.
5. Put in 3 quart greased baking dish, dot with bits of the margarine. Can be stored at refridgerator at this point if preparing ahead of time.
6. Bake for 1 hour at 350 degrees or until golden on top. Serve hot.
title: Colcannon

steps: 1. Using a biscuit cutter or round cookie cutter, cut out center of one slice of bread (discard center or save for another use). Spread mayonnaise on one side of bread slices. In a large skillet coated with cooking spray, lightly toast cutout slice, mayonnaise side down, over medium-low heat. Flip slice; crack an egg into center. Add remaining bread slice mayonnaise side down, to skillet; layer with cheese and bacon.

2. Cook, covered, until egg white is set, yolk is soft-set and cheese begins to melt. If needed, flip slice with egg to finish cooking. To assemble sandwich, use solid slice as bottom and cutout slice as top.
title: Toad In The Hole Bacon Sandwich

steps: 1. Mix everything, leaving butter for last.
2. Grease a flat bottomed frying pan or griddle.
3. Drop or pour small amounts of batter onto griddle.
4. Turn and cook other side when bubbles break on surface of crumpet.
5. Heat should be medium to get a deep, even golden colour.
6. Serve warm with butter and jam sandwiched together.
title: Easy Crumpets

ingredients.text: 1 1/4 lb. beef stew meat, cut into 1-inch pieces

steps: 1. Heat oil in large pot over medium-high heat.
2. Add beef and saute until well browned on all sides.
3. Add garlic and saute 1 minute.
4. Add beef broth, tomato paste, sugar, thyme, Worcestershire sauce, bay leaves and parsley.
5. Stir to combine. Bring mixture to a boil.
6. Reduce heat to medium-low; cover and simmer 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
title: Irish Beef Stew

steps: 1. Mix 3/4 cup flour in bowl with yeast and warm water. Blend until smooth, cover and leave until frothy, about 20 minutes.
2. Gradually stir other ingredients, beating until smooth. You should have a mixture like pancakes, or just a bit thicker. Add flour or water as necessary.
3. Heat a non-stick surface to med/med-high and put non-stick egg rings on surface to heat thoroughly.
4. Pour batter into rings, so it's about 1/2 in deep. Cook until dry on top, about 10 minutes.
5. Remove rings and turn crumpet over to brown on top. Cool on wire rack.
title: Whole Wheat Crumpets

ingredients.text: 1 whole Sweet Onion, Chopped Medium Fine
1/2 whole Cabbage, Shredded Finely As For Coleslaw (or 1 Package Angel Hair Shredded Cabbage)

steps: 1. Peel and quarter the potatoes and cover with water. Add salt. Bring to a boil and cook until fork-tender. Mash with 1/2 stick butter and 1/2 cup cream.

2. Meanwhile, melt remaining stick of butter in a skillet and add chopped onion and shredded cabbage. Reduce heat to low and cover skillet. Do not brown, just cook until onion is translucent. Stir mashed potatoes into cabbage-onion mixture and adjust seasonings.
3. Great with ham. Serves six.
title: Colcannon

steps: 1. Mix first 5 ingredients for about 5 minutes, cover with plastic wrap and let rise until doubled in bulk, about an hour.
2. Add salt, mix again, rise again.
3. Mix in baking soda and milk.

4. Heat pan to medium low. Butter crumpet rings (can use any 3-4 inch rings such as empty tuna cans with top and bottom remover, or commercial egg rings) and pan. Pour in just enough batter to fill the bottom of the ring.
5. Cook until brown on bottom and just set on top. There should be bubbles all over the top. Remove rings.
6. Turn briefly to cook the other side.
7. To serve, toast and spread with butter or jam.
title: English Crumpets

steps: 1. Melt butter.
2. Add cheese which has been cut into small pieces. Cook over hot water, stirring until cheese melts.
3. Add salt, mustard and Worcestershire sauce.
4. Pour in milk, slowly.
5. Add beaten eggs until mixture gets thick.
6. Serve over toast.
title: Welsh Rabbit

ingredients.text: 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, or as needed

steps: 1. Heat a heavy-bottomed skillet over medium heat.
2. Mix the self-rising flour and buttermilk together in a bowl until a workable dough forms; turn out onto a lightly floured work surface.
3. Pat the dough into a 1 1/2-inch thick round.
4. Cut the dough into 4 wedges.
5. Sprinkle enough all-purpose flour into the bottom of the skillet to lightly coat.
6. Cook the dough in the hot skillet until evenly browned and cooked through, about 8 minutes per side.
title: Irish Soda Farl

steps: 1. Preheat oven to 450 degrees.
2. Brown the sausages in a lightly greased frying pan for 10 minutes.
3. Stir and cook until well browned Sift together the dry ingredients and add milk, beat until a smooth batter.
4. Add the egges and beat.
5. Pour over the sausages and place in oven for 20 minutes.
6. Served with creamed onions or creamed corn.
title: Yorkshire Sausages

steps: 1. Spread peanut butter on 24 vanilla wafers cookies.
2. Top with remaining cookies to make sandwiches.
3. Melt butterscotch chips over double boiler.
4. Dip each cookie sandwich into melted butterscotch and place on waxed paper to cool.
5. Yield: 2 dozen "coins."
title: Pot Of "Irish Gold Coins"

steps: 1. Melt butter, seasonings and cheese in a double boiler until cheese is soft.
2. Add corn starch to beer and slowly add eggs to mixture. Cook until thick. Serve very hot on toast.
title: Welsh Rarebit

ingredients.text: 1 lb sausage (links or sliced patties, seasoned with sage or other herbs, OR vegetarian sausages, seasoned to your)

steps: 1. Pre-heat oven to 425 (220 C/ Gas 7).
2. Place butter and sausages in a 10" x 12" roasting pan.
3. Cook for 10 minutes, or until they are done to your liking.
4. Sift the flour into a bowl.
5. Break in the egg.
6. Gradually add half the milk, beating to form a smooth batter.
7. Pour in the remaining milk and beat until quite smooth.
8. Alternatively, add the flour, milk and egg to a blender or food processor and blend until smooth.
9. Pour the batter into the roasting pan and bake for 40-45 minutes, until the batter is well risen and golden.
title: Toad In The Hole

steps: 1. Put in blender and beat until mixed.
2. Keep refrigerated.
title: Irish Cream

steps: 1. Place all ingredients in a blender and mix until well blended. Refrigerate for up to 5 days.
title: Bailey'S Irish Creme

ingredients.text: 6 Cornish game hens (20 to 24 ounces each)

steps: 1. Place hens on a rack in a shallow baking pan. Tie legs with kitchen string if desired. Sprinkle with salt and pepper. Combine the butter, orange juice and honey; spoon over hens. Bake, uncovered, at 350° for 1 hour or until a thermometer reads 165° and juices run clear, basting every 15 minutes.

2. In a small saucepan, combine the orange juice, honey and vinegar. Combine cornstarch and water until smooth; stir into orange juice mixture. Bring to a boil; cook and stir for 1 minute or until thickened. Serve with hens.
title: Cornish Game Hens

steps: 1. Mix uncooked meat, vegetables and spices well together in a bowl.
2. Lay one pie crust flat on the lightly floured counter.
3. Put 1/4 of the filling mixture on one half of the crust, leaving at least a 1 1/2 inch area along the edge free for filling so that you can use this area for sealing.
4. Gently moisten the bottom edges on the sealing area with the milk using your fingertips.
5. Fold over the other half of the crust on top of the filling and bring the edges of the top half and the bottom half together and press to seal.
6. Fold the edges in towards the center once or twice.
7. Crimp the edges well.
8. Coat the entire top of the pastie with milk and place on a slightly greased large sheet pan.
9. Repeat with the other 3 crusts.
10. Bake for 425 degrees for about 15 minutes then reduce the temperature to 350 degrees for another 30 minutes, or until golden brown.
title: My Favorite Cornish Pasties

steps: 1. Heat fat in a large skillet.
2. Roll beef in flour and brown well in the hot fat; add enough water to cover and cook covered over low heat for 40 minutes, then add diced vegetables.
3. Mix well and add enough water to cover and cook covered slowly 40 minutes. Makes 4 generous servings.
title: Irish Stew

steps: 1. Cook rice and drain.
2. Flake the salmon.
3. Add to the rice and leave for 5 minutes to steam through.
4. Turn into a serving dish and sprinkle first with finely chopped parsley and then with chopped hard-boiled egg.
title: Kedgeree

steps: 1. Add flour to lukewarm milk.
2. Beat until smooth.
3. Add salt, butter and yeast.
4. Beat well.
5. Let rise until double.
6. Place greased muffin rings on hot griddle (1/2 fill with dough); cook until batter sets, then turn.
7. Makes 24 Crumpets.
title: English Crumpets

steps: 1. Brown meat while stirring constantly to break it into fine particles.
2. Add finely chopped onion, salt, pepper and water. Cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes.
3. Serve with boiled or mashed potatoes.
title: Scottish Mincemeat

steps: 1. Mix cocoa and coffee powders with Splenda.
2. Wet mixture with a bit of the whiskey to make a smooth paste.
3. Meanwhile, place cream in a heavy pan and cook on LOW heat until reduced to 2 1/2 cups.
4. Cool cream to room temperature.
5. Blend whiskey, paste, extracts and cream until smooth.
title: Low Carb Irish Cream

ingredients.text: 1 can (10-3/4 oz) condensed cream of chicken soup, undiluted

steps: 1. Saute onions in butter until tender. In a bowl combine soup, milk, pepper and two cups of the cheese. Stir in onions. Transfer to greased two quart baking dish and sprinkle with remaining cheese. Brush bread slices with melted butter on one side and place bread buttered side up over cheese. Bake uncovered at 350 for 25-30 minutes
title: Mrs. English'S Baked Onions

steps: 1. Clean celery, cut into one-inch pieces and place in a casserole dish.
2. Finely chop bacon and onion and sprinkle over celery along with chopped parsley.
3. Pour on stock. Dot with knobs of butter. Cover dish and bake in a moderate oven for 30-45 minutes.
title: Braised Celery (Irish)

steps: 1. Blend each ingredient as you add another.
2. Keeps well in refrigerator.
3. Serve over crushed ice.
4. Makes a nice substitute for dessert after a big dinner.
title: Bailey'S Irish Cream

ingredients.text: 14 ounces canned diced tomatoes, with juice

steps: 1. Put olive oil, garlic, tomatoes, and chili pepper in a large pot. Simmer 10 minutes.
2. Cook pasta, and when cooked, add the Romano cheese.
3. Mix the pasta in the pot with the sauce.
4. Add cilantro, cream, and vodka.
5. Simmer for another 10-15 minutes and serve.
title: Irish Vodka Pasta

ingredients.text: 6 tablespoons Butter, and or vegetable oil (butter tastes the best)

steps: 1. In a large frying pan melt the butter, make sure it doesn't brown. Add the finely chopped onion and fry gently for about 3 mins or until soft and translucent.

2. Turn the heat up ever so slightly and add the mashed potato and all of the chopped up leftover vegetables. Fry for at last 10 minutes turning them over continuously in the melted butter ensuring the potato and vegetables are thoroughly reheated. Plus you are also aiming to brown the outside edges of the vegetables but not to burning the bubble and squeak, so occasionally press the mixture onto the pan to brown a little then continue stirring.
3. Finally, when the mixture is heated right through, do one long final press. Press the potato mixture on to the base of the pan with a spatula and leave to cook for 1 min. Flip over and repeat.
4. Serve as mentioned above with either a fried or poached egg on top, the bacon pieces, or any leftover roast reheated thoroughly.
5. An alternative is to mix the potato and vegetables and form into small patties then fry as above.
title: Traditional Bubble And Squeak Recipe

steps: 1. Place hens on a wire rack in a large roasting pan. In a bowl, combine lemon juice, butter, paprika and tsp. thyme, seasoned salt and garlic powder. Pour half over the hens; set the remaining mixture aside for basting. Combine salt, pepper and remaining thyme, seasoned salt and garlic powder, sprinkle over the hens. Bake, uncovered at 375° for 30 minutes. Baste with remaining lemon mixture. Bake 30 minutes longer, basting occasionally, or until meat is tender and juices run clear.
title: Herbed Cornish Hens

steps: 1. Pour the milk, cream, and salt into a 3-quart stainless steel saucepan, and heat the milk to 190° F (88° C), stirring occasionally to keep it from scorching on the bottom. Remove from the heat and add the lemon juice, slowly stirring once or twice. Let the pot sit for 5 minutes. The milk will separate and form curds and whey.
2. Line a sieve with cheesecloth and place it over a large bowl. Pour the curds and whey into the sieve, and let strain for at least 1 hour.
3. Eat right away or transfer to an airtight container and refrigerate until ready to use. (Fresh ricotta will keep in the fridge for one week.)
title: Irish Farmhouse Ricotta

steps: 1. Place the brown sugar into a heavy bottomed saucepan.
2. Heat gently until the sugar has completely dissolved, but do not stir.
3. Boil to a temperature of 310°F (154°C) - measure with a candy thermometer for accuracy.
4. When the water has evaporated add a few drops of peppermint essence.
5. Pour mixture on a slab, using a knife to prevent it running too thin.
6. Cut into strips, and cut with sharp buttered scissors. If you pull it a bit before cutting with scissors it will turn a lovely amber color.
7. Wrap in cellophane and store in an airtight container.
title: Yorkshire Mint Humbugs

steps: 1. Salt the salmon steaks and set them aside.
2. Put half of the potatoes in the bottom of a heavy saucepan, cover with the sliced onion and top with the other half of potatoes. Cover the potatoes with boiling water and add one teaspoon of salt.
3. Bring the pan to a boil, cover and cook for 30 minutes. Five minutes before the cooking time is done, lay the salmon steaks on top of the potatoes and add salt and pepper to taste.
4. Return the soup to a boil and cover. The fish will cook thru in 5 minutes. Stir in the chives.
5. To make the butter sauce, melt the butter in a pan and stir in the vinegar and hardboiled chopped eggs.
6. Ladle the soup into bowls and serve with the butter sauce.
title: Scottish Tweed Kettle

ingredients.text: 1 medium onion, skinned and finely chopped

steps: 1. Melt the butter in a large frying pan. Add the onion and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring frequently, until softened.
2. Add the potatoes, cabbage and beef. Season to taste. Fry over medium heat for about 15 minutes, stirring frequently, until browned. Serve hot.
title: Bubble And Squeak

steps: 1. Dredge meat in seasoned flour.
2. Melt shortening in hot skillet and brown meat.
3. Reduce heat.
4. Add paprika, allspice, sugar, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, tomato juice and water.
5. Cover and cook over low heat for 1 1/2 hours.
6. Stir occasionally, adding more water if needed.
title: English Brown Stew

steps: 1. Melt butter; add flour, mustard, salt and Worcestershire sauce. Add milk and cook until thickened. Add cheese and cook until cheese is melted. Add egg and cook 3 minutes. Serve on toast. Sprinkle with paprika. Yield: 10 servings.
title: Welsh Rarebit

steps: 1. Place potatoes in a saucepan with enough water to cover. Bring to a boil, and cook for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender.

2. Place bacon in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium high heat until evenly brown. Drain, reserving drippings, crumble and set aside. In the reserved drippings, saute the cabbage and onion until soft and translucent. Putting a lid on the pan helps the vegetables cook faster.

3. Drain the cooked potatoes, mash with milk and season with salt and pepper. Fold in the bacon, cabbage, and onions, then transfer the mixture to a large serving bowl. Make a well in the center, and pour in the melted butter. Serve immediately.
title: Diane'S Colcannon

steps: 1. Mix condensed milk, chocolate syrup and eggs in a blender. While blender is running, add whiskey and vodka.
2. Blend thoroughly.
3. Refrigerate until used.
4. Yields 3 1/2 cups.
title: Barbara'S Irish Creme

steps: 1. Saute peas, almonds and mushrooms in butter approximately 10 minutes, until done. Salt and serve.
title: English Peas And Almonds

steps: 1. Place in blender and mix well.
2. Store in tightly covered jar. Keeps for 3 weeks in refrigerator.
title: Bailey'S Irish Cream

steps: 1. Preheat grill to medium high.
2. Cut Cornish hens in half lengthwise. Wash and pat dry.
3. Mix garlic powder, lemon pepper seasoning and paprika in a bowl.
4. Lift up skin and rub meat with seasoning mixture. Replace skin.
5. Cook on grill skin side down for 25 minutes, keeping grill lid closed.
6. Flip and cook for 15 minutes.
7. Mix lemon juice and olive oil. Brush on hens, then sprinkle with salt.
8. Cook for additional 10 minutes, or until internal temperature is 180°F.
title: Lemon Pepper Grilled Cornish Game Hens

ingredients.text: 2 1/2 pounds russet potatoes, peeled and cubed
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps: 1. Turn on a multi-functional pressure cooker (such as Instant Pot(R)) and select Saute function. Add 1 tablespoon butter and olive oil and allow butter to melt. Add cabbage and green onions and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes. Turn pot off.
2. Add potatoes and water to the pot. Close and lock the lid. Select manual pressure and set timer for 5 minutes. Allow about 10 minutes for pressure to build.
3. Release pressure carefully using the quick-release method according to manufacturer's instructions, about 5 minutes. Unlock and remove the lid.
4. Remove pressure cooker liner and place on the counter. Add milk and mash using a potato masher. Let colcannon stand for 3 minutes.
5. Transfer to a serving dish. Make a well in the center of the potatoes and add remaining 2 tablespoons butter. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
title: Instant Pot® Colcannon

steps: 1. Begin by roasting the squash. Slice it into thin crescents and drizzle with a little oil and sprinkle with sea salt. I added a fresh little sage I had in the fridge, but it’s unnecessary. Roast the squash a 205 C (400 F) for 20-30 minutes, flipping halfway through, until soft and golden. Let cool and chop into cubes.
2. Meanwhile, rinse the lentils and cover them with water. Bring them to the boil then turn down to a simmer and let cook (uncovered) for 20-30 minutes, or until tender. Drain and set aside.

3. While the lentils are cooking heat the 1 Tbsp. of oil on low in a medium pot. Add the onions and leeks and sauté for 5 or so minutes, or until they begin to soften. Add the garlic next along with the cumin and coriander, cooking for a few more minutes. Add the remaining spices – paprika, cinnamon, chilli, cocoa, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and oregano. Next add the can of tomatoes, the water or stock, and carrots. Let simmer, covered, for 20 minutes or until the veg is tender and the mixture has thickened up. You’ll need to check on the pot periodically for a stir and a top of of liquid if needed.
4. Add the lentils and chopped roasted squash. Let cook for 10 more minutes to heat through.
5. Serve with sliced jalapeno, lime wedges, cilantro, green onions, and cashew sour cream.
6. SIMPLE CASHEW SOUR CREAM
7. 1 Cup Raw Unsalted Cashews
8. Pinch Sea Salt
9. 1 tsp. Apple Cider Vinegar
10. Water

11. Bring some water to the boil, and use it to soak the cashews for at least four hours. Alternatively, you can use cold water and let the cashews soak overnight, but I’m forgetful/lazy, so often use the boil method which is much faster.

12. After the cashews have soaked, drain them and add to a high speed blender. Begin to puree, slowly adding about 1/2 cup fresh water, until a creamy consistency is reached. You may need to add less or more water to reach the desired consistency.
13. Add a pinch of sea salt and vinegar (or lemon juice).
title: Smoky Lentil Chili with Squash

ingredients.text: 2 cups rutabagas, finely chopped (you may substitute turnip)

steps: 1. Place all ingredients in a large pot, bring to the boil, then simmer for an hour.
2. Add more salt and pepper if desired.
title: Scottish Vegetable Soup

steps: 1. Boil the potatoes just until fork tender then drain and place them back in to the pot on low heat.
2. Add the butter, parsley and garlic; stir well to combine.
3. Serve hot and enjoy.
title: Irish Boiled Red Potatoes

ingredients.text: 2-1/2 pounds potatoes (about 6 medium), peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces

steps: 1. Place potatoes in a 6-qt. stockpot; add water to cover. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium; cook, covered, until potatoes are almost tender, 8-10 minutes.
2. Add cabbage and onion; cook, covered, until cabbage is tender, 5-7 minutes. Drain; return to pot. Add salt and pepper; mash to desired consistency, gradually adding butter and milk.
title: Colcannon Irish Potatoes

steps: 1. Cook potatoes in water until tender.
2. Drain.
3. While potatoes are cooking; Melt butter in large skillet.
4. Add chopped onion and cook for 5 minutes.
5. Stir in kale and cook 5 more minutes.
6. Remove from heat.
7. Mash potatoes, milk, sour cream, salt and pepper with mixer.
8. Stir in kale mixture.
title: Irish Mashed Potatoes (Colcannon)

ingredients.text: 1/4 cup vegetable oil (or enough to cover bottom of roasting pan)

steps: 1. Peel and quarter potatoes.
2. Place in a saucepan with water and a pinch of the salt.
3. Bring to a boil and simmer them for 5-6 mins to slightly soften.
4. Meanwhile preheat your oven to 400°F.
5. When the potatoes have simmered drain them thoroughly in a colander shaking to roughen edges.
6. Let sit for a few mins to dry.
7. Pour just enough vegetable oil into a roasting pan (large enough to allow space around the potatoes) to cover bottom and heat in oven for a few minutes.
8. Gently place potatoes into the hot oil and coat them with it evenly.
9. Sprinkle the salt and pepper over the potatoes.
10. Every so often baste the potatoes in the oil to prevent drying (try not to move potatoes).
11. Turn potatoes once or twice (no more) halfway through (after 20 mins or so) to ensure even cooking.
12. Cook for 30-60 mins until gold and crispy (observe closely once near end).
title: Perfect Traditionally English Roast Potatoes

steps: 1. Beat butter or margarine with corn syrup until blended, then work in the remaining ingredients and knead well.
2. Pinch off pieces just a bit smaller than walnuts and roll them between the palm of your hands.
3. With your thumb, flatten one side slightly, then make a few dents with a toothpick so the balls resemble little potato eyes.
4. Sprinkle a platter or piece of wax paper with cinnamon and roll potatoes until coated.
5. Be sure to cover dish with plastic wrap to minimize drying out.
6. Makes about 1 pound of candy.
title: Irish Cinnamon Potatoes

ingredients.text: 1/3 cup leek, cleaned and finely chopped (white end only)
3 slices whole wheat bread, fresh crumbs

steps: 1. In a large skillet cook the carrots, celery, leeks, mushrooms & onion in the 2 tbsp of butter (margarine) for about 3 minutes.
2. Add thyme, salt, pepper.
3. Mix bread crumbs with the veggies.
4. Cool mixture before stuffing birds.
title: Vegetable Stuffing For Cornish Game Hens

steps: 1. Peel potatoes and cut into 1/8-inch slices, combine mayonnaise, sour cream, horseradish, celery seed and salt.
2. Set aside.
3. Mix parsley and onion.
4. Arrange layer of potatoes and salt lightly.
5. Cover with mayonnaise mixture and layer of onion and parsley on top.
6. Do not stir.
7. Cover and let stand in refrigerator for 8 hours.
8. Bake 30 or 35 minutes in 350° oven.
title: Irish Potato Casserole

steps: 1. In a saucepan over medium heat, combine the sugar, butter, evaporated milk, cream of tartar and salt. Mix well and bring to a boil. Cook to the soft ball stage at 234 degrees F (115 degrees C). A few drops will form a soft ball when dropped into cold water. Remove from heat and cool to room temperature. Add vanilla and beat until creamy and stiff. Roll into balls and shape like little potatoes. Roll each ball in cinnamon to coat, then press in pieces of chopped nuts to look like eyes. You can also dust with cocoa to simulate dirt.
title: Grandmom'S Irish Potatoes

steps: 1. Preheat oven to 375°F.
2. In skillet, brown the ground beef and saute with onion.
3. Drain beef.
4. Stir in tomato sauce, salt, pepper, and celery salt.
5. Pour mixture into a 1.5 quart (8x10) dish.
6. Spread mashed potatoes over the beef mixture.
7. Sprinkle top with cheese.
8. Bake at 375°F for 30-35 minutes.
title: Shepherd'S Pie - A Beef And Mashed Potato Casserole

ingredients.text: 2 lbs carrots, peeled, sliced into discs

steps: 1. Melt butter.
2. Add carrots.
3. Cook for a minute.
4. Remove from heat.
5. Add whiskey OFF the stove.
6. Add brown sugar.
7. Return to stove.
8. Cook covered for 5 minutes or until carrots are as tender as you like them.
title: Irish Mist Whiskey Carrots

steps: 1. Melt one
2. stick
3. of
4. butter
5. and one cup of milk.
6. Pour over other
7. ingredients	and mix.
8. Pour in casserole dish and bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
title: Irish Potato Cheese Casserole

steps: 1. Mix ingredients together.
2. Roll into logs and chill.
3. Cut small pieces and shape into balls.
4. Roll balls in unsweetened cocoa powder, chopped nuts (any variety) or anything you might like. Spray Pam on them before rolling into whatever ingredients.
title: Irish Potato Candies

steps: 1. Combine sugar and butter in bowl.
2. Add egg white, milk, and vanilla to mixture.
3. Mix together until mixture is formed into ball.
4. Take small amount of mixture and form into little balls. Place cinnamon in a bowl and roll the balls (a few at a time) until they are evenly coated with cinnamon.
title: Irish Potatoes

steps: 1. Peel and cube potatoes; boil.
2. Mash and add remaining ingredients.
3. Sprinkle with paprika.
4. Use a 2-quart casserole. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
5. Take out of refrigerator; let sit 15 minutes.
6. Remove cover and bake at 350° for 1/2 hour.
title: Irish Potato Casserole

ingredients.text: 1 large ripe tomatoes (or two small tomatoes)
3 ounces feta cheese, drained and crumbled

steps: 1. Core and seed the tomatoes and cut into 1/4 inch dice. Peel and seed the cucumber and cut into 1/4 inch dice. Stem and seed the pepper and cut into 1/4 inch dice. Cut the onion into 1/4 inch dice.

2. Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, onion, parsley (if using) and most of the olives in a serving bowl. Add the oil, 1 tablespoon vinegar and salt and pepper and toss gently but thoroughly to mix. Correct the seasoning, adding salt and pepper or vinegar as necessary; the salad should be highly seasoned.
3. Sprinkle the crumbled feta cheese over the salad, decorate with the remaining olives and serve immediatley.
title: Shepherd'S Salad (Turkey)

steps: 1. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
2. In a large bowl, toss potato wedges and olive oil until the potatoes are coated. Spread the wedges out on a large baking sheet. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
3. Bake for 20 minutes in the preheated oven, turn over, and bake for an additional 10 to 15 minutes, or until tender. Serve plain, with vinegar, or dip in ketchup.
title: English Baked Potatoes

ingredients.text: 12 ounces lobsters, cooked, cut into 1/2-inch pieces

steps: 1. In a large bowl with a cover, mix together the lobster, cucumber, onion, celery & bell pepper, then season to taste with salt & pepper.
2. In a small bowl, whisk together the mayo, lime juice & hot pepper sauce, then pour this over the lobster mixture & toss carefully to combine.
3. Cover & chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour.
4. When ready, serve the lobster salad over a bed of salad greens & garnish with lemon slices.
title: Lobster Salad (British Virgin Islands -- Caribbean)

ingredients.text: 1/4 cup all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting

steps: 1. In a pot, cover potatoes with water and bring to a boil over high heat. Simmer on medium-high heat until the center of the potatoes are tender when pricked with a fork, about 20 minutes. Turn off heat. Drain, return potatoes to pot and allow to completely dry out over remaining heat. Mash with a potato masher until smooth.
2. Place warm mashed potato in medium bowl. Stir in flour, salt and melted butter. Mix lightly until dough forms.

3. On a well floured surface, knead the dough lightly. The dough will be sticky. Use a floured rolling pin to flatten into a 9 inch circle about 1/4 inch thick. Cut into quarters using a floured knife.
4. Sprinkle a little flour into the base of the skillet and cook the farls for 3 minutes on each side or until evenly browned. Season with a little salt and serve straight away.
title: Irish Potato Farls

steps: 1. Put in buttered casserole.
2. Bake 1 hour at 350°.
title: Irish Potato Casserole

steps: 1. Turn out hot potato pulp into a small bowl.
2. Add sugar, mashing it in. (Potato should be hot enough to melt sugar.)
3. Add vanilla and coconut and mix well.
4. Work mixture by kneading until it can be shaped more or less like a miniature potato.
title: Irish Potatoes

ingredients.text: 1 lb tart apple, peeled, cored and sliced

steps: 1. Cook potatoes in salted, boiling water until tender; drain well.
2. Meanwhile place apples in a pot with 1/3 cup of water and the sugar; cook at a simmer until soft.
3. Mash the cooked, drained potatoes thoroughly.
4. Mash in the cooked apples (with any remaining liquid), salt, pepper and butter.
title: Irish Apple Potato Mash

steps: 1. Peel the potatoes, cut into 1" chunks.Boil or steam the potatoes in salted water until fork tender, about 30 minutes. , drain.
2. Steam the cabbage, scallions, 1/4 cup water and 1/8 tsp.salt to boiling, reduce heat and cook until crisp-tender, about 10 minutes. Drain.
3. To the potatoes, add the milk, 1 teaspoons salt, pepper. and butter. Mash until smooth.
4. Stir in cabbage and scallions.
5. Dot with butter and serve. (Don't forget to tuck a coin in for luck!).
title: Colcannon (Mashed Potatoes With Cabbage)

steps: 1. Boil
2. potatoes	with
3. jackets
4. on.
5. Put in refrigerator until cool.
6. Peel.
7. Grate and add other ingredients.
8. Put into baking dish
9. and
10. bake in a 350° oven for 45 minutes or until cheese is melted.
title: Irish Potato Casserole

ingredients.text: 2 cups chopped kale, washed and stems removed.
2 large russet potatoes. Peeled, washed and cut into quarters
2 leeks, outer leaves removed, washed and finely chopped

steps: 1. 1.Remove the kale leaves from the tough stems. Wash and chop. Cook for a few minutes in boiling salted water until the leaves soften. Drain and set aside.

2. 2.Peel and wash the potatoes. Cut them into evenly sized quarters and put them in a saucepan. Just cover with cold, salted water. Bring to a boil over medium heat, then turn heat down, cover saucepan and simmer about ten minutes until the potatoes are soft when pierced with a fork but not mushy. Take saucepan off the heat. Drain the potatoes. Place them back in the saucepan. Cover the potatoes with a clean cotton dishtowel and cover saucepan. Place the saucepan over a very low heat for five minutes to dry the potatoes. Remove saucepan from heat.

3. 3.While the drained potatoes are drying over the low heat, place the chopped leeks and milk or cream in a small saucepan. Heat the milk, cook over a low heat for a few minutes to soften the leeks. Do not let the milk boil.
4. 4.Add the butter to the potatoes. Gradually add the milk and leek mixture (you may not need all of it) when mashing the potatoes.
5. 5.Blend in the cooked, chopped kale.
6. 6.The dish can be prepared in advance and kept warm, covered in the oven until ready to serve.
title: Kale With Buttery Mashed Potatoes And Leeks (Colcannon)

ingredients.text: 3 tablespoons scallions (I substitute onion on occasion)

steps: 1. Finely chop carrots, celery and scallions. Put them in the cup of water and simmer for 5 minutes. Reserve the vegetable and liquid for later.
2. Finely chop the small onion.
3. In a large pan, melt the butter and saute the onion until wilted.
4. Blend in flour, cook for a few minutes, then slowly add the chicken broth, whisking mixture constantly. Stir until thickened slightly.
5. Add the milk and vegetable mixture and bring to a boil.
6. Add the salt and pepper, dry mustard and cayenne pepper.
7. Grate the cheddar cheese and add the cheese to the mixture.
8. Stir until the cheese is melted and the soup is well blended.
9. Do not boil the soup after the cheese is added. You risk having the cheese separate.
title: English Cheddar Chowder (Cheese Soup)

steps: 1. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees. Line a roasting pan with foil.
2. Melt the butter and stir in 1/2 teaspoons salt and pepper, sage, onion, and celery. Cook until the veggies are soft, about 5 minutes. Add mushrooms and cook 3 minutes.
3. Stir in the stuffing and 1/4 cup water. Stir until absorbed and cool for 10 minutes.
4. Sprinkle the hens with the remaining salt and pepper. Fill the cavities of the hens with the stuffing and truss.
5. Roast until the meat thermometer in the thigh reads 180 degrees, about an hour and 15 minutes.
title: Cornish Game Hens With Sage Stuffing

steps: 1. Drain peas and add onions, peppers, cheese, celery and pickle relish.
2. Mix well and then toss gently with mayonnaise and egg. Chill.
title: English Pea Salad

ingredients.text: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps: 1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat; cook and stir the onions, carrots, celery, and garlic in the hot oil until the onions are translucent, 5 to 7 minutes.

2. Pour the vegetable stock into the pan and bring to a boil while scraping the browned bits of food off of the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. Season with the sage, salt, and black pepper. Reduce heat to low, place a cover on the pot, and cook until the flavors blend, about 1 hour.

3. Pour the soup into a blender pitcher to no more than half full. Hold the lid of the blender firmly in place. Carefully start the blender, using a few quick pulses to get the soup moving before leaving it on to puree. Puree in batches until smooth and pour into your serving vessel. Alternately, you can use a stick blender and puree the soup in the cooking pot.
title: Pota Brata (Irish Flag Soup)

steps: 1. Saute onions in butter and add potatoes, water and salt.
2. Cook until potatoes are tender.
3. Either mash or put in blender with the hot milk.
4. Slowly blend into mixture the cold milk and beaten yolk.
5. Add pepper and parsley.
6. Do not boil.
7. Serve with sharp Cheddar cheese, grated.
title: Irish Potato Soup

ingredients.text: 2 (15 ounce) cans English peas, well drained

steps: 1. Place peas in a large bowl.
2. Chop hard boiled eggs and add to peas along with the minced onion, pickle relish, and mayonnaise.
3. Stir gently to combine.
4. Chill until ready to serve.
title: English Pea Salad

steps: 1. Drain English peas.
2. Add chopped eggs.
3. Mix pimento and mayonnaise.
4. Chill and serve in a bed of lettuce or shredded purple cabbage.
title: English Pea Salad

ingredients.text: 1/2 cup butter, cut into thin slices
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps: 1. Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).
2. Arrange thinly sliced potatoes in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
3. Layer butter slices on top of potatoes. Season with salt and black pepper.
4. Pour half-and-half evenly over potato mixture.
5. Bake in preheated oven until sauce has thickened and potatoes are tender, 45 to 60 minutes.
title: Old Irish Scalloped Potatoes

steps: 1. Mix all ingredients, except corn flakes and oleo.
2. Melt oleo and add corn flakes.
3. Sprinkle on casserole and bake in 350° oven for 45 to 60 minutes.
title: Irish Potato Casserole

steps: 1. Heat the flat grill plate over a low heat, on top of 2 rings/flames if it fits, and brush sparingly with light olive oil.

2. Cook the sausages first. Add the sausages to the hot grill plate/the coolest part if there is one and allow to cook slowly for about 15-20 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden. After the first 10 minutes, increase the heat to medium before beginning to cook the other ingredients. If you are struggling for space, completely cook the sausages and keep hot on a plate in the oven.

3. Snip a few small cuts into the fatty edge of the bacon. Place the bacon straight on to the grill plate and fry for 2-4 minutes each side or until your preferred crispiness is reached. Like the sausages, the cooked bacon can be kept hot on a plate in the oven.

4. For the mushrooms, brush away any dirt using a pastry brush and trim the stalk level with the mushroom top. Season with salt and pepper and drizzle over a little olive oil. Place stalk-side up on the grill plate and cook for 1-2 minutes before turning and cooking for a further 3-4 minutes. Avoid moving the mushrooms too much while cooking, as this releases the natural juices, making them soggy.

5. For the tomatoes, cut the tomatoes across the centre/or in half lengthways if using plum tomatoes , and with a small, sharp knife remove the green 'eye'. Season with salt and pepper and drizzle with a little olive oil. Place cut-side down on the grill plate and cook without moving for 2 minutes. Gently turn over and season again. Cook for a further 2-3 minutes until tender but still holding their shape.
6. For the black pudding, cut the black pudding into 3-4 slices and remove the skin. Place on the grill plate and cook for 1½-2 minutes each side until slightly crispy.
